LEU is the cleanest US-listed mid-cap mapping to HALEU enrichment and should remain in the underfollowed fuel-cycle lane, but survival in later layers depends on evidence of scale-up beyond DOE demonstration quantities.
FLS is a second-order nuclear-qualified component candidate hidden inside diversified flow-control machinery; verify nuclear backlog and project-level wins before upgrading.
ASPI belongs in speculative_shadow rather than core underfollowed until enrichment permits, technical validation, financing drawdowns, and facility construction evidence improve.

Need a separate pass for private or foreign-listed bottleneck suppliers in nuclear forgings, deconversion, conversion, zirconium/alloys, ASME N-stamp fabrication, QA/testing labs, and EPC subcontractors; many true bottlenecks may not be US-listed pure plays.

node: Nuclear fuel cycle, HALEU/enrichment, nuclear-grade components, and advanced-reactor qualification
summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: This node expands into two public exposure clusters: fuel-cycle bottlenecks and qualified nuclear hardware. The cleanest direct bottleneck name is Centrus (HALEU/enrichment). The clearest component suppliers are BWXT and Cameco's fuel-services chain. Constellation is the demand-side asset-owner anchor that helps validate whether the buildout is moving from headlines to committed load-serving projects. Expanded the universe around scarce nuclear fuel-cycle and nuclear-grade component chokepoints rather than reactor-developer headlines. The pass found one direct HALEU/enrichment reference name, two less-obvious qualified component suppliers, and one small-cap speculative fuel-cycle exception. The strongest public evidence clusters around DOE HALEU enrichment awards, long qualification cycles for nuclear valves/pumps/control systems, and advanced-reactor fuel fabrication partnerships. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Layer 1B expands the underfollowed stock universe around nuclear fuel and nuclear-grade components tied to AI/data-center firm-power demand. The main chokepoint candidates are not only reactor developers, but HALEU enrichment, TRISO/fuel fabrication, deconversion, qualification testing, and nuclear-qualified pumps/valves/components. This pass keeps one reference anchor, BWXT, and prioritizes smaller or less directly labeled names such as LEU, FLS, and ASPI. Several claims remain hypotheses because hyperscaler nuclear announcements still need to convert into binding offtake, fuel orders, DOE/NRC milestones, and funded capacity expansion
